steps.extra: Some would say it’s a waste of money.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Some would say it’s a waste of ___." (~ 낭비라고 하는 사람도 있을 거예요.). When to use it: 내 생각이 아니라 반대쪽 의견을 공정하게 소개해요. a waste of + 명사. Note: Some would say it’s a waste of money.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "The benefits aren’t always obvious.".

steps.title: Look Up · 11월 첫 토요일 밤, 아파트 옥상에서 별을 보며

lines.en: Look, that tiny light moving across the sky. Is it a plane?
lines.ko: 저기 봐요, 하늘을 가로지르는 작은 불빛. 비행기예요?

lines.en: It’s not blinking, so I think it’s a satellite.
lines.ko: 깜박이지 않으니까 인공위성 같아요.

lines.en: Wow. I watched a rocket launch video last night. It gave me chills.
lines.ko: 와. 어젯밤에 로켓 발사 영상을 봤는데 소름이 돋았어요.

lines.en: It’s amazing, but {{some would say it’s a waste of}} money. We have problems to solve here first.
lines.ko: 멋지긴 한데, 돈 낭비라는 사람도 있을 거예요. 지구에서 먼저 풀 문제가 있으니까요.

lines.en: Tell me more. Why do you think so?
lines.ko: 더 얘기해 봐요. 왜 그렇게 생각해요?

lines.en: The costs are astronomical, and many people still can’t afford a home. A space mission won’t fix that.
lines.ko: 비용이 엄청나고, 아직 집을 못 구하는 사람도 많아요. 우주 탐사가 그걸 해결하진 않죠.

lines.en: Fair. But {{the benefits aren’t always obvious.}} Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts.
lines.ko: 맞아요. 그래도 이점이 늘 바로 보이진 않아요. 인공위성 덕에 GPS와 일기 예보가 있잖아요.

lines.en: True. Our bike-sharing app wouldn’t even work without GPS.
lines.ko: 맞네요. 우리 공유 자전거 앱도 GPS 없이는 아예 안 돌아가요.

lines.en: And it inspires the next generation. My niece wants to be an astronaut.
lines.ko: 그리고 다음 세대에게 꿈을 줘요. 제 조카는 이제 우주 비행사가 되고 싶대요.

lines.en: That’s sweet. But some people say humanity needs a backup plan, like colonizing Mars. That sounds far-fetched to me.
lines.ko: 귀엽네요. 그런데 인류에게 화성 정착 같은 비상 계획이 필요하다는 건 지금으로선 너무 비현실적인 얘기 같아요.

lines.en: Me too, for now. So what’s your view? Say it like you mean it.
lines.ko: 저도 지금은 그래요. 그래서 지우 씨 생각은요? 진심을 담아 말해 봐요.

lines.en: {{In the grand scheme of things,}} we’re a tiny dot in the universe. Curiosity drives progress. It’s not either-or. We can fix things here and keep exploring.
lines.ko: 크게 보면 우린 우주의 작은 점이에요. 호기심이 발전을 이끌어요. 둘 중 하나가 아니에요. 여기 문제도 고치고 탐사도 계속하면 돼요.

lines.en: Now that’s an answer! I want to hear that in client meetings.
lines.ko: 바로 그거예요! 고객 회의에서 그렇게 말하는 걸 듣고 싶어요.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Look Up · 11월 첫 토요일 밤, 아파트 옥상에서 별을 보며", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Maya: "Look, that tiny light moving across the sky. Is it a plane?" (저기 봐요, 하늘을 가로지르는 작은 불빛. 비행기예요?)
2. Jiwoo: "It’s not blinking, so I think it’s a satellite." (깜박이지 않으니까 인공위성 같아요.)
3. Maya: "Wow. I watched a rocket launch video last night. It gave me chills." (와. 어젯밤에 로켓 발사 영상을 봤는데 소름이 돋았어요.)
4. Jiwoo: "It’s amazing, but some would say it’s a waste of money. We have problems to solve here first." (멋지긴 한데, 돈 낭비라는 사람도 있을 거예요. 지구에서 먼저 풀 문제가 있으니까요.)
5. Maya: "Tell me more. Why do you think so?" (더 얘기해 봐요. 왜 그렇게 생각해요?)
6. Jiwoo: "The costs are astronomical, and many people still can’t afford a home. A space mission won’t fix that." (비용이 엄청나고, 아직 집을 못 구하는 사람도 많아요. 우주 탐사가 그걸 해결하진 않죠.)
7. Maya: "Fair. But the benefits aren’t always obvious. Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts." (맞아요. 그래도 이점이 늘 바로 보이진 않아요. 인공위성 덕에 GPS와 일기 예보가 있잖아요.)
8. Jiwoo: "True. Our bike-sharing app wouldn’t even work without GPS." (맞네요. 우리 공유 자전거 앱도 GPS 없이는 아예 안 돌아가요.)
9. Maya: "And it inspires the next generation. My niece wants to be an astronaut." (그리고 다음 세대에게 꿈을 줘요. 제 조카는 이제 우주 비행사가 되고 싶대요.)
10. Jiwoo: "That’s sweet. But some people say humanity needs a backup plan, like colonizing Mars. That sounds far-fetched to me." (귀엽네요. 그런데 인류에게 화성 정착 같은 비상 계획이 필요하다는 건 지금으로선 너무 비현실적인 얘기 같아요.)
11. Maya: "Me too, for now. So what’s your view? Say it like you mean it." (저도 지금은 그래요. 그래서 지우 씨 생각은요? 진심을 담아 말해 봐요.)
12. Jiwoo: "In the grand scheme of things, we’re a tiny dot in the universe. Curiosity drives progress. It’s not either-or. We can fix things here and keep exploring." (크게 보면 우린 우주의 작은 점이에요. 호기심이 발전을 이끌어요. 둘 중 하나가 아니에요. 여기 문제도 고치고 탐사도 계속하면 돼요.)
13. Maya: "Now that’s an answer! I want to hear that in client meetings." (바로 그거예요! 고객 회의에서 그렇게 말하는 걸 듣고 싶어요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

1. Maya: "Look, that tiny light moving across the sky. Is it a plane?" (저기 봐요, 하늘을 가로지르는 작은 불빛. 비행기예요?)
2. Jiwoo: "It’s not blinking, so I think it’s a satellite." (깜박이지 않으니까 인공위성 같아요.)
3. Maya: "Wow. I watched a rocket launch video last night. It gave me chills." (와. 어젯밤에 로켓 발사 영상을 봤는데 소름이 돋았어요.)
4. Jiwoo: "It’s amazing, but some would say it’s a waste of money. We have problems to solve here first." (멋지긴 한데, 돈 낭비라는 사람도 있을 거예요. 지구에서 먼저 풀 문제가 있으니까요.)
5. Maya: "Tell me more. Why do you think so?" (더 얘기해 봐요. 왜 그렇게 생각해요?)
6. Jiwoo: "The costs are astronomical, and many people still can’t afford a home. A space mission won’t fix that." (비용이 엄청나고, 아직 집을 못 구하는 사람도 많아요. 우주 탐사가 그걸 해결하진 않죠.)
7. Maya: "Fair. But the benefits aren’t always obvious. Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts." (맞아요. 그래도 이점이 늘 바로 보이진 않아요. 인공위성 덕에 GPS와 일기 예보가 있잖아요.)
8. Jiwoo: "True. Our bike-sharing app wouldn’t even work without GPS." (맞네요. 우리 공유 자전거 앱도 GPS 없이는 아예 안 돌아가요.)
9. Maya: "And it inspires the next generation. My niece wants to be an astronaut." (그리고 다음 세대에게 꿈을 줘요. 제 조카는 이제 우주 비행사가 되고 싶대요.)
10. Jiwoo: "That’s sweet. But some people say humanity needs a backup plan, like colonizing Mars. That sounds far-fetched to me." (귀엽네요. 그런데 인류에게 화성 정착 같은 비상 계획이 필요하다는 건 지금으로선 너무 비현실적인 얘기 같아요.)
11. Maya: "Me too, for now. So what’s your view? Say it like you mean it." (저도 지금은 그래요. 그래서 지우 씨 생각은요? 진심을 담아 말해 봐요.)
12. Jiwoo: "In the grand scheme of things, we’re a tiny dot in the universe. Curiosity drives progress. It’s not either-or. We can fix things here and keep exploring." (크게 보면 우린 우주의 작은 점이에요. 호기심이 발전을 이끌어요. 둘 중 하나가 아니에요. 여기 문제도 고치고 탐사도 계속하면 돼요.)
13. Maya: "Now that’s an answer! I want to hear that in client meetings." (바로 그거예요! 고객 회의에서 그렇게 말하는 걸 듣고 싶어요.)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/틀려요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. Do all 3 statements, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: Some would say it’s a waste of ___.
In the grand scheme of things, ___.
head: 주제
Some would say it’s a waste of …
But in the grand scheme of things, …
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Some would say it’s a waste of ___. / In the grand scheme of things, ___. Table (주제 → Some would say it’s a waste of …):
- space missions → money.
- a giant telescope → money.
- studying the stars → time.
- long research projects → time.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items: It’s worth ~ · It’s a waste of ~

It’s *worth* explor*ing*. 탐사할 가치가 있어요. (worth + -ing/명사) 
It’s *a waste of* money. 돈 낭비예요. (a waste of + 명사) 
Some would say it’s a waste of money, but I think *it’s worth it*.
In the grand scheme of things

크게 보면, 전체 그림에서 보면 
*In the grand scheme of things*, one bad day doesn’t matter. 크게 보면 하루 안 좋은 건 별일 아니에요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- It’s worth ~ · It’s a waste of ~: It’s worth exploring. 탐사할 가치가 있어요. (worth + -ing/명사) / It’s a waste of money. 돈 낭비예요. (a waste of + 명사) / Some would say it’s a waste of money, but I think it’s worth it.
- In the grand scheme of things: 크게 보면, 전체 그림에서 보면 / In the grand scheme of things, one bad day doesn’t matter. 크게 보면 하루 안 좋은 건 별일 아니에요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- It’s worth to explore space. → It’s worth exploring space. (worth 뒤에는 -ing.)
- It’s waste of money. → It’s a waste of money. (a waste of로 써요.)
- The benefits isn’t always obvious. → The benefits aren’t always obvious. (benefits(복수)라서 aren’t.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: It’s worth ~ · It’s a waste of ~: It’s worth exploring. 탐사할 가치가 있어요. (worth + -ing/명사) It’s a waste of money. 돈 낭비예요. (a waste of + 명사) Some would say it’s a waste of money, but I think it’s worth it.
In the grand scheme of things: 크게 보면, 전체 그림에서 보면 In the grand scheme of things, one bad day doesn’t matter. 크게 보면 하루 안 좋은 건 별일 아니에요.
mistakes: It’s worth to explore space. → It’s worth exploring space.
It’s waste of money. → It’s a waste of money.
The benefits isn’t always obvious. → The benefits aren’t always obvious.

steps.note: 예) space research / money → A: Some would say space research is a waste of money. B: Maybe, but I think it’s worth it.
steps.teach:
Situation drill. Note on screen: 예) space research / money → A: Some would say space research is a waste of money. B: Maybe, but I think it’s worth it. Items (situation → model answer): space research → money | a giant telescope → money | learning Latin → time | video games → time.
Give them one at a time as a tiny situation in simple English and let the learner answer. Recast once if needed. Keep it lively, with a quick natural reaction to each answer. After all items, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Then call finish_session.

cards: Some would say it’s a waste of ___.
In the grand scheme of things, ___.
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "In the grand scheme of things" (우주 탐사); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Some would say it’s a waste of ___." / "The benefits aren’t always obvious." / "In the grand scheme of things, ___.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: We have problems to solve here first.
Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts.
인공위성 덕분에 GPS와 일기 예보가 있어요.
It’s a matter of national pride.
둘 중 하나만 고를 문제가 아니에요.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 아쉬워하는 쪽: "We have problems to solve here first." (여기서 먼저 풀 문제가 있어요., 보통); "The costs are astronomical." (비용이 천문학적이에요., 보통); "Private companies are taking over." (민간 기업이 주도권을 잡고 있어요., 보통)
- 가치 있다는 쪽: "Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts." (인공위성 덕분에 GPS와 일기 예보가 있어요., 보통); "It inspires the next generation." (다음 세대에게 꿈을 줘요., 보통); "Curiosity drives progress." (호기심이 발전을 이끌어요., 정중); "Humanity needs a backup plan." (인류에게는 비상 계획이 필요해요., 보통); "It’s a matter of national pride." (나라의 자부심이 걸린 일이에요., 보통)
- 정리하기: "It’s not either-or." (둘 중 하나만 고를 문제가 아니에요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: (참고) 확실한 말로 바꾸기

Space research gave us GPS and much more.라고 말하는 사람도 있지만, 여기서는 개발 기원 전체를 단정하지 않고 지금 위성의 쓰임을 말해요. 
확실한 말 → Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts.
덩어리 표현

*by virtue of* its size 그 크기 덕분에(격식 있는 말) 
There’s no *turning back*. 되돌아갈 수 없어요. · *turn back* 되돌아가다
steps.blank:
A: Is space exploration worth the money?   B: Some would say it’s a ___ of money. 
A: But the benefits aren’t always ___.   B: True. In the grand ___ of things, it’s worth it. 
낱말 상자: waste · obvious · scheme
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- (참고) 확실한 말로 바꾸기: Space research gave us GPS and much more.라고 말하는 사람도 있지만, 여기서는 개발 기원 전체를 단정하지 않고 지금 위성의 쓰임을 말해요. / 확실한 말 → Satellites give us GPS and weather forecasts.
- 덩어리 표현: by virtue of its size 그 크기 덕분에(격식 있는 말) / There’s no turning back. 되돌아갈 수 없어요. · turn back 되돌아가다
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Is space exploration worth the money? B: Some would say it’s a ___ of money. / A: But the benefits aren’t always ___. B: True. In the grand ___ of things, it’s worth it. / 낱말 상자: waste · obvious · scheme
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: space ((지구 대기 밖) 우주 공간), universe (우주(별과 은하를 포함한 모든 것)), satellite (인공위성), astronaut (우주 비행사), mission ((우주) 임무, 탐사 계획), exploration (탐사, 탐험), discovery (발견), colonize ((새 땅에) 정착지를 세우다(역사에서는 ‘식민지로 만들다’)), frontier ((아직 잘 모르는) 미개척 분야, 최전선), innovation (혁신, 새로운 기술·방법), investment (투자), humanity (인류).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: private (민간의, 개인의) — "private companies"; astronomical (천문학의; (값이) 천문학적인, 엄청난) — "astronomical costs"; inspire (영감·의욕을 주다) — "It inspires kids."; budget (예산) — "a huge space budget"; progress (발전, 진보) — "Curiosity drives progress."; curiosity (호기심) — "endless curiosity"; telescope (망원경) — "look through a telescope"; launch ((로켓) 발사; 발사하다) — "a rocket launch".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Is space exploration worth the money? Why or why not?
Some would say it’s a waste of ___, but ___.
What’s something whose benefits aren’t always obvious?
The benefits of ___ aren’t always obvious. For example, ___.
When you look at the night sky, what do you think about?
In the grand scheme of things, ___.
If you could go to space, would you?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Is space exploration worth the money? Why or why not?" (hint on screen: Some would say it’s a waste of ___, but ___.)
- "What’s something whose benefits aren’t always obvious?" (hint on screen: The benefits of ___ aren’t always obvious. For example, ___.)
- "When you look at the night sky, what do you think about?" (hint on screen: In the grand scheme of things, ___.)
- "If you could go to space, would you?" (hint on screen: I’d love to ___. / No way. ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: One Year of Saturdays
steps.text: It had been almost a year since the first Saturday dinner at Grace’s place. After cake, the six friends went up to the rooftop with blankets. Daniel spotted another satellite, and Ben joked that it was checking on their dinner. Chloe asked who would take a one-way ticket to Mars. “There’s no *turning back*,” she warned. Nobody raised a hand. Grace said the universe, *by virtue of* its sheer size, will always leave room for new discoveries. Later, Maya pulled Jiwoo aside. “Next year, you’ll lead the meetings with our overseas client yourself,” she said. Jiwoo’s eyes went wide. “You already have the ideas,” Maya said. “Let’s practice speaking formally, and still sounding like you.” Jiwoo looked up at the stars and nodded.
steps.gloss: one-way 편도의 · turn back 되돌아가다 · by virtue of ~ 덕분에 · sheer 순전한, 엄청난 · pull aside 따로 불러내다 · formally 격식 있게
questions: What did Chloe ask the group?
What will Jiwoo do next year?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "One Year of Saturdays". Text: "It had been almost a year since the first Saturday dinner at Grace’s place. After cake, the six friends went up to the rooftop with blankets. Daniel spotted another satellite, and Ben joked that it was checking on their dinner. Chloe asked who would take a one-way ticket to Mars. “There’s no turning back,” she warned. Nobody raised a hand. Grace said the universe, by virtue of its sheer size, will always leave room for new discoveries. Later, Maya pulled Jiwoo aside. “Next year, you’ll lead the meetings with our overseas client yourself,” she said. Jiwoo’s eyes went wide. “You already have the ideas,” Maya said. “Let’s practice speaking formally, and still sounding like you.” Jiwoo looked up at the stars and nodded." Words: one-way 편도의 · turn back 되돌아가다 · by virtue of ~ 덕분에 · sheer 순전한, 엄청난 · pull aside 따로 불러내다 · formally 격식 있게.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What did Chloe ask the group?" / "What will Jiwoo do next year?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Some would say it’s a waste of ___.’로 반대쪽 의견을 공정하게 소개할 수 있어요.
‘The benefits aren’t always obvious.’로 잘 보이지 않는 이점을 말할 수 있어요.
‘In the grand scheme of things, ___.’로 크게 보며 의견을 정리할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Some would say it’s a waste of ___.’로 반대쪽 의견을 공정하게 소개할 수 있어요.
- ‘The benefits aren’t always obvious.’로 잘 보이지 않는 이점을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘In the grand scheme of things, ___.’로 크게 보며 의견을 정리할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Then call finish_session.
